ES.name: Amor seco / Amos seco
ES.citation: RAE - Diccionario historico del espanol de Canarias. Canary Islands Spanish usage, documented since at least 1799 (Viera y Clavijo). Stage 1 range-triage had marked Spain 'no evidence' - this corrects that omission. CAUTION: 'amor seco' and its variants are shared across several burr-bearing Asteraceae in Spanish (the RAE source itself groups it with 'brujilla'/'lapsana') - this specific attribution is species-specific per the cited source, but the generic term is not exclusive to Bidens pilosa
